title: Sunday jam sessions on 52nd Street
summary: Milt Gabler's Sunday afternoon sessions were among the first advertised, open jam sessions, unlike the casual Harlem sessions.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But when you were in...like in New York, in the days right after you left Basie, and you used to sit in quite a
bit, sessions like that... When they start appearing? Like, when did musicians get together for sessions and stuff?

Well, Milt Gabler used to have them. But he'd hire guys, you know. But now and then, extra guys would come and sit in, too. This would be on Sunday afternoons. Milt Gabler was one of the instigators of the first....those kind of things.
But there must have been sessions before that...
Well, there had been in Harlem a lot of jam sessions, you know. But they weren't like specialty jam sessions, you know.
Yes, it just happened. But this is an affair that was advertised, jam sessions -- you know?
Right. Well, they were open to the public, so to speak.
